newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end stronger on extended golds rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end stronger on extended golds rally.

text.p: Toronto stocks closed stronger in moderate trading on Friday, helped by an extended rally in heavyweight golds.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 21.88 points to 6226.95 on turnover of 136.07 million shares worth C$1.97 billion.
"The interest with the gold sector is still occupying a lot of attention," said ScotiaMcLeod senior vice-president Fred Ketchen.
Bullion prices continued to bounce back from recent lows. April COMEX rose $1.50 an ounce to close at $354.10.
Of Toronto's 14 sub-indices, only two -- retail and banks -- failed to rise. Golds led the gainers, followed by conglomerates, transportation and forestry products.
Advancing issues outpaced declines 587 to 434 and another 280 traded flat.
Over the week Canada's largest equities market only rose 21 points from Monday's open, trading in a relatively narrow range.
In individual issues, prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd. lost 1.50 to reach 21.20 after investors tried to sort through this week's news.
Shares in Petro-Canada, the integrated oil company, slipped 0.20 to 20.20 on turnover of 14.1 million.
